note: Canonical Carefield facility types. These are regulatory universes, not marketing labels. A facility may hold several (e.g. a dually certified SNF/NF). Source-native program and type labels are always kept alongside.

types.label: Skilled nursing facility (SNF)
types.definition: Certified by CMS to participate in Medicare as a skilled nursing facility (42 CFR Part 483).

types.label: Nursing home (NF)
types.definition: Certified to participate in Medicaid as a nursing facility. Many sites are dually certified SNF/NF.

types.label: Assisted living
types.definition: State-licensed residential setting with personal care and supervision. Definitions vary by state.

types.label: Memory care
types.definition: Usually a state license endorsement or service designation for dementia care, not a standalone facility class.

types.label: Residential care facility
types.definition: State-licensed residential care for older adults, e.g. California RCFE.

types.label: Adult care home
types.definition: State-licensed adult home / adult care facility, e.g. North Carolina adult care homes, New York adult homes.

types.label: Personal care home
types.definition: State-licensed personal care home, e.g. Pennsylvania PCH (distinct from PA assisted living residences).

types.label: Adult family home
types.definition: Small state-licensed residential home, e.g. Washington or Wisconsin AFH.

types.label: Continuing care retirement community (CCRC)
types.definition: Campus offering a continuum of housing and care under a continuing-care contract. Regulation varies by state.

types.label: Independent living
types.definition: Age-restricted housing without licensed care. Often little structured public data.

types.label: Other senior residential care
types.definition: Senior residential care that fits no other canonical type.
